rundown: Tigers beat Jaguars 54-52 at Coliseo Guillermo Angulo in Carolina, Puerto Rico in front of 250. Tigers came back: they were down 29-27 at the half. The 3rd quarter decided it: Tigers won it 14-8. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 76%).
Leading the way — Tigers: Jessica Peterson 13 pts, 13 reb; Sania Richardson 4 ast. Jaguars: DeMya Porter 14 pts, 9 reb; Deniya Thornton 3 ast.
Where Tigers won it: they shot 43% to 40% and won the boards 36-27.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 26, 9:57 AM ET. It had Tigers 95% and Jaguars 5%, projecting Tigers 71.7 – Jaguars 50.1 (121.8 total, Tigers by 21.6).

Final: Tigers 54 – Jaguars 52. Right winner: it had Tigers at 95%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Tigers came in with a 5% above average attack and a 12% stingier than average defense (6-1, 70 scored and 54 allowed a game over 7 games), worth about 163 and 163 games of evidence. Projected to score 71.7, they scored 54 (−17.7 points, 25% under); projected to allow 50.1, they allowed 52 (+1.9 points, 4% over).

Jaguars came in with a 10% below average attack and a 2% leakier than average defense (1-5, 50.2 scored and 78.5 allowed a game over 6 games), worth about 172 and 177 games of evidence. Projected to score 50.1, they scored 52 (+1.9 points, 4% over); projected to allow 71.7, they allowed 54 (−17.7 points, 25% under).

The bigger miss was Tigers' scoring (-17.7 points against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 106 against 121.8 projected (-15.8), about the 13th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14).

Margin: Tigers by 2 against Tigers by 21.6 projected, about the 93rd percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±13).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body: No line was priced for this game (no posted odds, or not enough data to price one).

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; there were no odds to check the projection against.

The projection missed by a lot, so those flags likely mattered here.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.846 of the raw projection. It counts toward NCAAW scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 1101 graded NCAAW games the algo now scales scoring ×0.971 and gives home teams +1.3 points. Team corrections so far: Tigers attack ×0.989, defense ×0.985 (7 games); Jaguars attack ×0.977, defense ×0.985 (6 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 19.6 points), no bet.
